newsitem.title: USA: CME, others to announce electronic trading pact.
newsitem.headline: CME, others to announce electronic trading pact.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said it would unveil on Thursday an agreement on common electronic trading and clearing for six international exchanges.

In a statement, the exchange said officials from the CME and the New York Mercantile Exchange would make an announcement on a letter of intent involving a "revolutionary global exchange technology swap." A CME spokesman declined to disclose which other exchanges were involved.
Asked if the agreement would be on a system to replace the GLOBEX electronic futures and options trading system, the spokesman said without elaborating, "Potentially."

Earlier this month, Reuters Holdings Plc said GLOBEX, which it had developed with the CME and France's MATIF futures exchange, was unlikely to continue operating beyond 1998, when the current contract expires.
MATIF said last month it was switching from GLOBEX to a new system it was developing with SBF, the French stock exchanges association.
